date_note: SecurityWeek, published November 18, says Google announced the release on Tuesday (November 17).
title: Chrome 158 fixes 204 vulnerabilities, six rated critical
summary: Google released Chrome 158 for Windows, macOS and Linux with fixes for 204 vulnerabilities: 6 critical, 62 high, 82 medium and 54 low. Use-after-free is the most common type (51). No exploitation in the wild is mentioned. Google found 145 itself and paid $11,000 for five external reports.
plain: Google released a very large Chrome security update, with six serious flaws fixed. No attacks are reported.
exec: A big routine browser patch; no known exploitation, but six critical flaws are fixed.
action: Update Chrome to 158.0.8127.36 or later and restart browsers; check managed fleets pick up the update.

key_findings: Fixed in 158.0.8127.36/.37; no in-the-wild exploitation mentioned.
